newsitem.title: UK: Broad EMU expectations move higher - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Broad EMU expectations move higher - JP Morgan.

text.p: Expectations of a broad-based start to European economic and monetary union (EMU) were higher in the past week, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed on Friday.

Of the ten European countries monitored by JP Morgan, only Portugal registered a decline in its chances of joining the single currency at its start, according to JP Morgan's "EMU calculator", which is derived from the interest-rate swaps market.
Portugal's first wave EMU prospects dipped to 76 percent from 79 percent in the previous week.
The probability of France and Belgium joining Germany in monetary union on schedule in 1999 was unchanged from last week at 100 percent.
Italy's perceived chances of entering EMU were up at 79 percent from a 74 percent rating last week, while Spain's rose to 83 from 81 percent.

Britain, viewed as the least likely country to join EMU at its start, saw its probability rise to 27 percent from 23 percent. Ireland's chances, meantime, went up to 67 percent against 61 percent a week ago.
JP Morgan said there was a reasonable margin of error in overall probability levels of less than five percentage points on average.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
